cells.tense: The heart is open today and you're letting it stay that way.
cells.ask: Tell one person something you might be feeling, and leave it at maybe.
cells.core: You let a feeling form before you name it. Most people either close up or grab the first thing that comes through and turn it into a verdict. You're doing neither, and that's the trick of this place — following the pull toward a person or a room before you know why, without making it mean something yet. It also means sitting in the unfinished part while nothing is settled, and not reaching for a label to stop the discomfort. That patience is the cost, and you're paying it. Stay with one thing you can't name yet and let it stay unnamed.
cells.sheetLine: Open is a place to stand, not a stop along the way.
cells.verb: opening to feel what hasn't arrived yet
cells.place: the moment before a choice splits into one thing

cells.tense: You are bracing for what this open door will cost before it has cost anything at all.
cells.ask: Pick one thing and finish it by Friday, then stop rehearsing how it ends.
cells.core: Walking through an open door at your own pace, feeling something new without scripting the ending — that's the version that works. Yours is a waiting room. Something could start and you're already past it, planning the ending, the fallout, what you'll do when it turns. The bracing has become the activity. A finished thing under your feet steadies an open feeling, keeps it from lurching ahead of itself. Get one end in by Friday. The feeling will still be here when you come back, and it won't need a plan running alongside it.
cells.sheetLine: You're living past a door that's still swinging open.

cells.tense: You are standing in a doorway you walked away from a long time ago.
cells.ask: Go somewhere new this week with no plan and let it land however it lands.
cells.core: Beginner's mind — arriving somewhere like it's the first time, letting a thing reach you before you've sorted it. That's the working version. Lately nothing gets to land first. You decide too fast, or leave before it can reach you, and the handling of rooms and people and plans keeps rolling. None of them touch you. What ran dry isn't the ability; it's the freshness, the open stance that makes a moment new. Don't push for more feeling on command — that goes into a place that's empty. Do one small thing with no outcome attached and let it be unimpressive. A shut door comes back by letting one new thing stay new.
cells.sheetLine: The door isn't locked. You just stopped walking through.

cells.tense: You are opening to things all day and calling it something other than your own doing.
cells.ask: Name one feeling you had this week and say that it belonged to you.
cells.core: Receiving without erasing yourself: you notice what lands and you know you're the one it landed on. That's the version that works, and yours is close to it. A feeling arrives, you catch it, you let it shape how you answer, and then you describe it as if it came from nowhere, or as if you were just being sensible. Somebody has to be here for a feeling to land on, and that somebody is you. Start with the ordinary: a song that hit, a comment that stuck, a mood you carried home. Calling that background is how you lose credit for your own part. Claim one small arrival this week and say it was yours.
cells.sheetLine: The feeling landed on you. You're the one who was open.

attempts.check: The record doesn't say the vessel ever actually opened — it says 'opened before anything has been poured,' which is a readiness, not an event; so I must not claim this person has already received something and it went wrong. A reader could reasonably say 'nothing bad ever happened, I just haven't started anything yet,' and they'd be right about the history, just not about the seat. The ask survives being wrong because it's a genuine opening move either way, not a repair. The sentence that serves me more than them is any where I get to sound knowing about what's underneath — I'll keep the verbs as plain moves a person could do today.
